tone_patterns: Formal, institutional tone emphasizing accountability, oversight, and role clarity
Process-oriented language that describes how governance operates (inputs, approvals, monitoring, validation)
Neutral, descriptive phrasing that avoids promotional adjectives except when briefly contextualizing programs
Frequent use of governance and risk-management terminology to signal alignment with recognized practices
paragraph_patterns: Subsection opens with a short framing paragraph stating purpose and scope of the roles being described
Role descriptions follow a consistent pattern: who the group is, what they do, who they collaborate with, and what outputs they produce
Responsibilities are presented as multi-clause sentences listing actions (e.g., define, monitor, propose, validate, approve) in a logical sequence
Use of clarifying parentheticals to define acronyms or alternative terms for the same entity
Occasional inclusion of an illustrative example (e.g., a program) to demonstrate how governance translates into operational activity
heading_patterns: Numbered subsection headings (e.g., 2.x) paired with a descriptive title focused on 'Role of…'
Standalone section header 'Governance' repeated as a running section identifier
Diagram/table title uses an integration framing (e.g., 'Integration of…') to introduce a model depiction
Committee/working-group subsection uses a heading that distinguishes 'additional' bodies from decision-making bodies
table_patterns: Three-column comparative layout aligned to a recognized governance model (e.g., first/second/third line), with each column containing role narratives
Column headers are short and categorical; body text is paragraph-style rather than bullet-only
Within each column, multiple functions may be separated into distinct paragraphs to avoid overly dense blocks
Consistent use of role verbs and responsibility statements across columns to enable easy comparison
figure_or_diagram_patterns: Model-based governance diagram/table introduced by a single-sentence lead-in explaining why the model matters
Use of a named governance framework as the organizing visual concept
Visual emphasizes lifecycle/oversight flow conceptually, while detailed responsibilities remain in adjacent text blocks
pdf_layout_patterns: Page header/footer pattern includes section name, page number, and report title line as repeating elements
Section label appears near the bottom or margin as a navigational cue, separate from main body text
Multi-page continuity: subsection text begins on one page and transitions to a model layout on the next page
Use of wide, columnar layout for the governance model page to fit parallel role descriptions
Committee/working-group page uses a two-part layout: descriptive paragraphs on top with a structured list of bodies below
disclosure_language_patterns: Clear delineation between decision-making authority and supporting/advisory roles
Approval chain language presented in escalating order (propose → validate → approve), indicating governance escalation
References to alignment with external frameworks and local guidelines stated as compliance-oriented commitments
Use of scope qualifiers and exclusions to define boundaries of responsibility (e.g., what is included vs excluded)
Forward-looking phrasing used cautiously to indicate planned incorporation of evolving topics, tied to regulatory/industry evolution
evidence_presentation_patterns: Governance effectiveness supported through references to established models (e.g., lines of defence) rather than performance claims
Mentions of periodic updates, monitoring activities, and internal review functions as procedural evidence
Cross-references to other report sections for deeper detail, keeping governance section focused on roles and oversight
Inclusion of internal control and independent assurance-like functions (e.g., audit) as credibility mechanisms
section_specific_observations: Governance narrative is organized by organizational layers: working team roles → enterprise risk model integration → additional committees
Strong emphasis on collaboration interfaces between sustainability function, risk management, finance, compliance, and audit
Explicit separation of operational execution (business units) from oversight (risk/compliance) and independent assurance (audit)
Committee descriptions use a consistent 'are responsible for' structure and focus on methodology/policy approvals
things_to_avoid_copying: Any organization-specific team names, committee names, acronyms, or branded program names
Any claims of awards, program outcomes, or qualitative impact statements tied to specific initiatives
Any references to specific regulators, local guideline names, or jurisdiction-specific standards as-is
Any detailed descriptions of proprietary frameworks, scorecards, or internal policy titles
Any explicit scope statements that include specific emissions categories or calculation exclusions as written
content_specific_items_detected_and_excl: Named sustainability team and executive roles and their approval hierarchy
Named risk management model and its specific implementation framing
Specific internal committees and forums (including oversight and methodology approval bodies)
References to specific policies, frameworks, scorecards, and stress testing practices
References to emissions scopes and financed-emissions boundary statements
Mentions of a branded volunteering/community program and award reference
References to specific regulatory guidelines and jurisdictional bodies
